entities.name: Red reef lobster
entities.fact: Unlike true spiny lobsters, reef lobsters carry small pincers on their first three pairs of legs.

entities.name: Southern king crab
entities.fact: The southern king crab lives in the cold waters around Tierra del Fuego and is fished for its large, meaty claws and legs.

entities.name: Golden king crab
entities.fact: Golden king crabs live on the cold continental slope of the North Pacific and are caught in deep traps.

entities.name: Atlantic rock crab
entities.fact: The Atlantic rock crab lives along the shores of eastern North America and crushes small shellfish in its strong claws.

entities.name: Oilfish
entities.fact: The flesh of the oilfish is rich in waxy esters that humans cannot digest, causing oily diarrhoea, and its sale is banned in Japan.

entities.name: Mangrove horseshoe crab
entities.fact: The mangrove horseshoe crab can carry tetrodotoxin and has caused fatal poisonings when eaten in South-East Asia.

entities.name: Toxic reef crab
entities.fact: Cooking does not destroy the saxitoxin and tetrodotoxin in this brightly marked Indo-Pacific reef crab, which has killed people who ate it.

entities.name: Japanese ivory shell
entities.fact: The salivary glands of this edible sea snail contain surugatoxin, which caused outbreaks of poisoning in Japan in the 1960s.

entities.name: Shortfin mako
entities.fact: Shortfin makos keep their bodies warmer than the surrounding water, which powers their famous bursts of speed.

entities.name: Pallid sturgeon
entities.fact: The pallid sturgeon of the Missouri and Mississippi rivers is a pale, shovel-snouted giant listed as endangered in the United States.

entities.name: Kaluga
entities.fact: The kaluga of the Amur river basin is one of the largest freshwater fish in the world and is critically endangered.

entities.name: Devils Hole pupfish
entities.fact: The Devils Hole pupfish lives in a single water-filled limestone cave pool in Nevada, one of the smallest ranges of any vertebrate.

entities.name: Pineapplefish
entities.fact: The pineapplefish has yellow, black-edged scales that resemble a pineapple's skin and carries glowing bacteria in organs on its lower jaw.

entities.name: Peanut worm
entities.fact: When disturbed, a peanut worm pulls its narrow front end into its body, leaving a shape like a peanut.

entities.name: Butterfish
entities.fact: The butterfish of the North Atlantic coast is a small, silvery, oily fish named for its soft, buttery flesh.

entities.name: Sea potato
entities.fact: The sea potato is a heart urchin that lives buried in sand and is named for its rounded, potato-like shape.

entities.name: Sea pork
entities.fact: Sea pork is a colonial sea squirt that forms fleshy lumps, and its name comes from a resemblance to salted pork.

entities.name: Egg-yolk jellyfish
entities.fact: The egg-yolk jellyfish has a yellow-orange centre inside a clear bell and feeds mostly on other jellyfish.

entities.name: Cabbage head jellyfish
entities.fact: The cabbage head jellyfish drifts in warm Indo-Pacific waters, and its frilly arms resemble a cabbage or cauliflower.

entities.name: Lemon peel angelfish
entities.fact: The lemon peel angelfish takes its name from its bright lemon-yellow body, which is marked with a blue ring around the eye.

entities.name: Banana prawn
entities.fact: Banana prawns take their name from their yellowish colour and are a main catch of prawn trawlers in northern Australia.

entities.name: Strawberry anemone
entities.fact: The strawberry anemone is a red anemone of rocky shores whose green-flecked column looks like a strawberry.

entities.name: Strawberry conch
entities.fact: The strawberry conch is a reef snail with a pink-orange shell opening and eyes on long stalks.

entities.name: Chocolate surgeonfish
entities.fact: Young chocolate surgeonfish mimic dwarf angelfish, while adults are chocolate brown with an orange patch behind the gill.

entities.name: Date mussel
entities.fact: The date mussel, shaped like a date fruit, bores into limestone using chemical secretions.

entities.name: Mustard hill coral
entities.fact: Mustard hill coral forms yellow-brown mounds and is one of the most common reef-building corals of the Caribbean.

entities.name: Candy crab
entities.fact: The candy crab lives on soft corals of the genus Dendronephthya and copies their pink and white colours as camouflage.

entities.name: Chicken liver sponge
entities.fact: The chicken liver sponge is a smooth, dark-brown encrusting sponge named for its colour and texture.

entities.name: Breadcrumb sponge
entities.fact: The breadcrumb sponge grows as crumbly yellow-green crusts on rocky shores of the North Atlantic.

entities.name: Butter clam
entities.fact: Butter clams of the Pacific North-west can hold paralytic shellfish toxins in their siphons for a very long time.

entities.name: Lollipop catshark
entities.fact: The lollipop catshark is a small deep-water shark of the eastern Pacific with a broad, rounded head like a lollipop.

entities.name: Queen conch
entities.fact: The queen conch has a heavy shell with a flared pink lip and has been a staple food of the Caribbean for centuries.

entities.name: King scallop
entities.fact: King scallops have a row of tiny eyes along the edge of their mantle and swim by clapping their two shells together.

entities.name: Queen scallop
entities.fact: Queen scallops, smaller than king scallops, escape danger by clapping their shells to jet through the water.

entities.name: King prawn
entities.fact: King prawns such as the western king prawn are large, commercially important prawns of Australian waters.

entities.name: Queenfish
entities.fact: The queenfish is a fast, silvery fish of Indo-Pacific shallows that often leaps clear of the water while chasing prey.

entities.name: Emperor snapper
entities.fact: Young emperor snappers wear bold dark bars across a pale body, and the bars fade as they grow into red adults.

entities.name: Queen snapper
entities.fact: The queen snapper is a bright red, large-eyed snapper of the deep Atlantic reef slope.

entities.name: Queen coris
entities.fact: The queen coris is an Indian Ocean wrasse whose colour and pattern change dramatically as it grows from juvenile to adult.

entities.name: King ragworm
entities.fact: The king ragworm is a large marine worm that can grow well over half a metre long and is dug by anglers for bait.

entities.name: King helmet
entities.fact: The king helmet is a heavy-shelled Caribbean sea snail that feeds on sea urchins and sand dollars.

entities.name: Queen helmet
entities.fact: The queen helmet is a large sea snail that feeds on sea urchins and whose thick shell has been carved into cameos.

entities.name: Emperor bream
entities.fact: Emperor breams of the family Lethrinidae are Indo-Pacific reef fish with strong jaws for crushing hard-shelled prey.

entities.name: King eider
entities.fact: Male king eiders have a bright orange shield on the bill, and the species dives for food in cold Arctic seas.

entities.name: King shag
entities.fact: The king shag is a rare cormorant that breeds only in the Marlborough Sounds of New Zealand.

entities.name: Yellowtail kingfish
entities.fact: Yellowtail kingfish are fast, powerful predators that are both farmed and prized by sport anglers in the southern hemisphere.

entities.name: King threadfin
entities.fact: The king threadfin of northern Australia begins life as a male and changes into a female as it grows older.

entities.name: Blue king crab
entities.fact: The blue king crab is a cold-water crab of the North Pacific and Bering Sea and a close relative of the red king crab.

entities.name: Kingklip
entities.fact: Kingklip is a long, slender cusk-eel of southern African waters that is prized as food.

entities.name: Northern kingfish
entities.fact: The northern kingfish is a bottom-feeding member of the drum family found along the Atlantic coast of North America.

entities.name: Southern kingfish
entities.fact: The southern kingfish is a bottom-feeding member of the drum family found along the western Atlantic coast.

entities.name: Spangled emperor
entities.fact: The spangled emperor is a widespread Indo-Pacific reef fish and a popular catch for anglers.

entities.name: Longnose emperor
entities.fact: The longnose emperor is an Indo-Pacific reef fish with a long, pointed snout.

entities.name: Pink ear emperor
entities.fact: The pink ear emperor is a small emperor named for the pinkish patch on its gill cover.

entities.name: Yellowlip emperor
entities.fact: The yellowlip emperor is a large Indo-Pacific emperor with bright yellow lips.

entities.name: Thumbprint emperor
entities.fact: The thumbprint emperor carries a dark blotch on its flank and feeds on sandy flats and seagrass beds around reefs.

entities.name: Sky emperor
entities.fact: The sky emperor is an emperor of the western Indian Ocean that lives around reefs and is fished for food.

entities.name: Orange-striped emperor
entities.fact: The orange-striped emperor is an Indo-Pacific reef fish marked with orange stripes along its flanks.

entities.name: King George whiting
entities.fact: King George whiting is a prized food fish of southern Australia, named after King George Sound in Western Australia.

entities.name: Cockatoo waspfish
entities.fact: The cockatoo waspfish rocks gently like a drifting leaf, and its tall dorsal fin carries venomous spines.

entities.name: Owl limpet
entities.fact: The owl limpet tends a private patch of algae on its rock and bulldozes away intruders that threaten it.

entities.name: Partridge tun
entities.fact: The partridge tun is a large sea snail with a thin, speckled shell patterned like a partridge's plumage.

entities.name: Pheasant shell
entities.fact: The pheasant shell is a glossy Australian sea snail whose colourful pattern resembles a pheasant's plumage.

entities.name: Hawkwing conch
entities.fact: The hawkwing conch is a small Caribbean conch whose shell lip flares out like a wing.

entities.name: Turkey wing ark
entities.fact: The turkey wing ark is a zebra-striped bivalve that anchors itself to rocks with a tuft of tough threads.

entities.name: Cock's comb oyster
entities.fact: The cock's comb oyster has a zigzag shell edge like a rooster's comb and lives fixed to coral and rock.

entities.name: Pelican's foot
entities.fact: The pelican's foot is a small European sea snail whose shell lip spreads into webbed fingers like a pelican's foot.

entities.name: Peacock worm
entities.fact: The peacock worm lives in a tube and spreads a fan of feathery tentacles to catch food particles from the water.

entities.name: Dove snail
entities.fact: Dove snails of the family Columbellidae are small sea snails, often with brightly patterned shells.

entities.name: Canary rockfish
entities.fact: The canary rockfish is a bright orange fish of the North American Pacific coast that was heavily overfished and then rebuilt.

entities.name: Short-tailed albatross
entities.fact: The short-tailed albatross was feared extinct in the 1940s before a few breeding birds were found on a Japanese island.

entities.name: Tufted puffin
entities.fact: The tufted puffin breeds around the North Pacific and grows golden head plumes during the breeding season.

entities.name: Yellow-eyed penguin
entities.fact: The yellow-eyed penguin, or hoiho, is one of the world's rarest penguins and nests in coastal forest and scrub in southern New Zealand.

entities.name: Red-billed tropicbird
entities.fact: The red-billed tropicbird has two very long central tail feathers and plunge-dives for flying fish and squid.

entities.name: Northern fulmar
entities.fact: The northern fulmar defends itself and its chick by spitting a foul-smelling stomach oil at intruders.

entities.name: Red-footed booby
entities.fact: The red-footed booby is the smallest booby and, unlike its relatives, usually nests in trees and bushes.

entities.name: Wedge-tailed shearwater
entities.fact: Wedge-tailed shearwaters nest in burrows on Pacific islands and make eerie moaning calls at night.

entities.name: Sooty tern
entities.fact: Sooty terns can spend years at sea after fledging, rarely landing on the water, before returning to breed.

entities.name: Little penguin
entities.fact: The little penguin of Australia and New Zealand stands only about 30 centimetres tall and is the smallest penguin.

entities.name: Black-browed albatross
entities.fact: Black-browed albatrosses have a dark smudge over each eye and breed in huge colonies, mainly on the Falkland Islands.

entities.name: Bermuda petrel
entities.fact: The Bermuda petrel, or cahow, was thought extinct for about three centuries until a few nesting pairs were rediscovered in 1951.

entities.name: Bay scallop
entities.fact: Bay scallops have dozens of tiny blue eyes along their mantle and swim by snapping their shells shut.

entities.name: Yesso scallop
entities.fact: The Yesso scallop is intensively farmed in Japan and China and is one of the most widely cultured scallops.

entities.name: Mediterranean mussel
entities.fact: The Mediterranean mussel has spread to coasts around the world and is widely farmed for food.

entities.name: Black-lip pearl oyster
entities.fact: The black-lip pearl oyster produces the dark pearls known as Tahitian pearls.

entities.name: Common cockle
entities.fact: The common cockle burrows in sandy European shores and can leap away from danger by flicking its muscular foot.

entities.name: Olympia oyster
entities.fact: The Olympia oyster is a small, coin-sized oyster native to the Pacific coast of North America.

entities.name: Thorny oyster
entities.fact: Thorny oysters are spiny, brightly coloured bivalves whose shells were treasured by ancient Andean peoples.

entities.name: Angelwing
entities.fact: The angelwing is a bivalve whose long white shell resembles a pair of wings and which bores into mud and clay.

entities.name: Piddock
entities.fact: The common piddock bores into soft rock and clay and is famously bioluminescent.

entities.name: Windowpane oyster
entities.fact: The windowpane oyster has a thin, translucent shell that was once used in place of glass in windows in parts of Asia.

entities.name: File clam
entities.fact: The file clam builds a nest of shell and gravel held together by threads and waves long, orange tentacles.

entities.name: Flame scallop
entities.fact: The flame scallop flashes its mantle edge so that it seems to flicker like a light.

entities.name: Horse mussel
entities.fact: Horse mussels form dense beds in cold northern seas that shelter many other animals.

entities.name: Bear paw clam
entities.fact: The bear paw clam is a giant clam with a thick, ridged shell that gets part of its food from algae living in its tissues.

entities.name: Fluted giant clam
entities.fact: The fluted giant clam has ruffled scales on its shell and gets much of its food from algae living in its tissues.

entities.name: Toheroa
entities.fact: The toheroa is a prized New Zealand surf clam that is now heavily protected.

entities.name: Peruvian scallop
entities.fact: The Peruvian scallop is farmed along the coasts of Peru and Chile.

entities.name: Atlantic sea scallop
entities.fact: The Atlantic sea scallop supports a major fishery off the north-eastern United States.

entities.name: Coquina
entities.fact: Tiny coquina clams repeatedly dig in and out of the sand as waves wash up the beach.

entities.name: Pismo clam
entities.fact: The Pismo clam is a large clam of the Californian coast named after Pismo Beach.

entities.name: Atlantic ribbed mussel
entities.fact: The Atlantic ribbed mussel lives in salt marshes, wedged among the roots of cordgrass.

entities.name: Jingle shell
entities.fact: Jingle shells are thin, translucent bivalves that cement themselves to rocks and other shells and chime when they are strung together.

entities.name: Tuatua
entities.fact: The tuatua is a New Zealand surf clam traditionally gathered from sandy beaches.

entities.name: Pacific gaper
entities.fact: The Pacific gaper is a large clam whose long siphon is too big to pull back inside its shell.

entities.name: Shipworm
entities.fact: Shipworms are bivalves with long, worm-like bodies that bore through wood and once threatened wooden ships.

entities.name: Sea slug
entities.fact: Sea slugs are marine snails that have lost or shrunk their shell, and many are brightly coloured to warn predators of their toxins.

entities.name: California sea hare
entities.fact: The California sea hare has unusually large nerve cells, which made it a model animal for memory research that earned a Nobel Prize.

entities.name: Hooded nudibranch
entities.fact: The hooded nudibranch spreads a large, fringed hood like a net to trap small crustaceans drifting past.

entities.name: Clown nudibranch
entities.fact: The clown nudibranch is a white sea slug with orange-tipped bumps that feeds on bryozoans along the Pacific coast of North America.

entities.name: Frosted nudibranch
entities.fact: The frosted nudibranch has white-tipped, feathery gills and can swim by flexing its body from side to side.

entities.name: Gaudy nudibranch
entities.fact: The gaudy nudibranch is a large, brightly coloured sea slug of Indo-Pacific reefs with a ridge along its back.

entities.name: Orange peel nudibranch
entities.fact: The orange peel nudibranch is a large, bumpy orange sea slug of the north-eastern Pacific.

entities.name: Hopkins' rose nudibranch
entities.fact: Hopkins' rose is a bright pink, fuzzy-looking sea slug of the Pacific coast of North America that feeds on bryozoans.

entities.name: California blue dorid
entities.fact: The California blue dorid is a deep-blue sea slug marked with yellow, found along the Pacific coast of North America.

entities.name: Crested nembrotha
entities.fact: The crested nembrotha is a large, boldly coloured Indo-Pacific sea slug that feeds on sea squirts.

entities.name: Anna's chromodoris
entities.fact: Anna's chromodoris is a blue nudibranch with a yellow-edged mantle that grazes on sponges on Indo-Pacific reefs.

entities.name: Willan's chromodoris
entities.fact: Willan's chromodoris is a colourful reef nudibranch of the western Pacific that grazes on sponges.

entities.name: Kunie's chromodoris
entities.fact: Kunie's chromodoris is a brightly coloured sea slug of Indo-Pacific reefs that grazes on sponges.

entities.name: Bullock's nudibranch
entities.fact: Bullock's nudibranch is a purple Indo-Pacific sea slug with orange gills that feeds on sponges.

entities.name: Varicose phyllidia
entities.fact: The varicose phyllidia is a black sea slug with yellow-tipped bumps that makes toxic chemicals to deter predators.

entities.name: Sap-sucking slug
entities.fact: The sap-sucking slug keeps the chloroplasts of the algae it eats and uses them to photosynthesise for weeks.

entities.name: Wedge sea hare
entities.fact: The wedge sea hare is a large Indo-Pacific sea slug that gave chemists dolastatins, compounds studied as anti-cancer drugs.

entities.name: Glass sea slug
entities.fact: The glass sea slug is a transparent, free-swimming sea slug that drifts in open water and glows when disturbed.

entities.name: Navanax
entities.fact: The navanax hunts other sea slugs by following their slime trails across the seabed.

entities.name: Spotted sea hare
entities.fact: The spotted sea hare of European coasts is named for its ear-like tentacles, and it can release a cloud of purple ink.

entities.name: Swimming eolid
entities.fact: The swimming eolid houses algae in its feathery gills and can swim by wriggling its body.

entities.name: Homberg's tritonia
entities.fact: Homberg's tritonia is a large cold-water sea slug of the north-east Atlantic that feeds on soft corals called dead man's fingers.

entities.name: Berghia
entities.fact: Berghia sea slugs eat glass anemones, and aquarists keep them to control those pests.

entities.name: Janolus cristatus
entities.fact: Janolus cristatus is a sea slug with a bushy crest on its head that feeds on bryozoans.

entities.name: White Atlantic cadlina
entities.fact: The white Atlantic cadlina is a small white sea slug of cold North Atlantic water that feeds on sponges.

entities.name: Barnacle-eating nudibranch
entities.fact: The barnacle-eating nudibranch specialises in feeding on acorn barnacles in cold northern seas.

entities.name: Fourlined polycera
entities.fact: The fourlined polycera is a small sea slug of North Atlantic shores that feeds on bryozoans.

entities.name: Olive nudibranch
entities.fact: The olive nudibranch eats sea anemones and keeps their stinging cells for its own defence.

entities.name: Common grey sea slug
entities.fact: The common grey sea slug eats sea anemones and stores their stinging cells in the tips of its gills.

entities.name: Rainbow dendronotid
entities.fact: The rainbow dendronotid is one of the largest nudibranchs of the Pacific coast and has branching, frilly gills.

entities.name: Orange-clubbed sea slug
entities.fact: The orange-clubbed sea slug of North Atlantic shores has orange-tipped, club-shaped projections along its body.

entities.name: Verco's nudibranch
entities.fact: Verco's nudibranch is a brightly coloured sea slug of southern Australian coasts that feeds on bryozoans.

entities.name: Phyllodesmium longicirrum
entities.fact: Phyllodesmium sea slugs feed on soft corals and house algae in their long, feathery gills.

entities.name: Painted blue dorid
entities.fact: The painted blue dorid is a blue sea slug with yellow lines found from the Mediterranean to the Canary Islands.

entities.name: Green-lined paper bubble
entities.fact: The green-lined paper bubble is a sea slug with a thin, delicate bubble-like shell marked with fine green lines.

entities.name: Glaucilla
entities.fact: Glaucilla floats at the sea surface and preys on other drifting animals such as blue buttons.

entities.name: California Pleurobranchaea
entities.fact: The California Pleurobranchaea is a predatory sea slug studied for how a simple nervous system makes decisions.

entities.name: Elysia timida
entities.fact: Elysia timida is a Mediterranean sea slug that keeps chloroplasts from the algae it eats and uses them to make sugars.

entities.name: Leaf sheep
entities.fact: The leaf sheep is a tiny sea slug that keeps chloroplasts from the algae it eats, and its green gills give it the look of a miniature sheep.

entities.name: Black mangrove
entities.fact: Black mangroves push pencil-like roots up out of the mud to breathe and get rid of salt through their leaves.

entities.name: White mangrove
entities.fact: White mangroves have two small glands at the base of each leaf stalk that secrete excess salt.

entities.name: Grey mangrove
entities.fact: The grey mangrove has the widest range of any mangrove, growing from East Africa to New Zealand and south-eastern Australia.

entities.name: Shoal grass
entities.fact: Shoal grass is a thin-bladed seagrass of the western Atlantic that is often the first to colonise shallow, disturbed sand.

entities.name: Manatee grass
entities.fact: Manatee grass has round, noodle-like leaves and is grazed by manatees and sea turtles in the Caribbean.

entities.name: Surfgrass
entities.fact: Surfgrass clings to rocky shores of the north-eastern Pacific and withstands pounding surf rather than rooting in sand.

entities.name: Tape seagrass
entities.fact: Tape seagrass is among the largest seagrasses of the Indo-Pacific, with ribbon-like leaves that can be a metre or more long.

entities.name: Nipa palm
entities.fact: The nipa palm is a mangrove palm with a creeping, partly underground trunk whose sap is tapped to make sugar and vinegar.

entities.name: Buttonwood
entities.fact: Buttonwood grows on the landward edge of mangrove forests and gets its name from its small, button-like clusters of fruit.

entities.name: Little Neptune grass
entities.fact: Little Neptune grass forms seagrass meadows in the Mediterranean and along the neighbouring Atlantic coast.

entities.name: Asiatic mangrove
entities.fact: The Asiatic mangrove props itself on stilt roots and drops long, pencil-shaped seedlings that are already germinated.

entities.name: Dwarf eelgrass
entities.fact: Dwarf eelgrass grows on the muddy flats of European coasts and is a favourite food of brent geese.

entities.name: Noodle seagrass
entities.fact: Noodle seagrass has round, needle-like leaves and grows in meadows across the Indo-Pacific.

entities.name: Narrowleaf seagrass
entities.fact: Narrowleaf seagrass has three-pointed leaf tips and is an important food of dugongs.

entities.name: Paddle weed
entities.fact: Paddle weed has small, oval leaves on slender stalks and is a favourite food of dugongs.

entities.name: Johnson's seagrass
entities.fact: Johnson's seagrass, found only on Florida's east coast, was the first marine plant listed as threatened under the United States Endangered Species Act.

entities.name: Wire weed
entities.fact: Wire weed of southern Australia has woody stems topped with tufts of leaves and forms tall underwater meadows.

entities.name: Rimurehu
entities.fact: Rimurehu is the Maori name for the eelgrass that forms the main seagrass meadows of New Zealand and southern Australia.

entities.name: Thalassia hemprichii
entities.fact: Thalassia hemprichii is the Indo-Pacific cousin of turtle grass, with sickle-shaped leaves grazed by green turtles and dugongs.

entities.name: Large-leafed orange mangrove
entities.fact: Bruguiera gymnorrhiza sends knee-like roots looping up out of the mud so that the tree can take in air.

entities.name: Cannonball mangrove
entities.fact: The cannonball mangrove is named for its heavy, round fruit, which looks like a cannonball.

entities.name: Mangrove apple
entities.fact: Sonneratia alba is a pioneer mangrove whose flowers open at night and are pollinated by bats and moths.

entities.name: River mangrove
entities.fact: The river mangrove is a shrubby mangrove that excretes salt through its leaves and has curved, horn-shaped seedlings.

entities.name: Sundri
entities.fact: The sundri is thought to have given the Sundarbans mangrove forest its name, and it is now an endangered tree.

entities.name: Spotted mangrove
entities.fact: The spotted mangrove grows on stilt roots along the coasts of northern Australia and the western Pacific.

entities.name: Tall-stilt mangrove
entities.fact: The tall-stilt mangrove is a major source of timber and charcoal in the mangrove forests of South-East Asia.

entities.name: Milky mangrove
entities.fact: The milky mangrove has a sap that can badly irritate the eyes, which earned it the nickname blind-your-eye.

entities.name: Spurred mangrove
entities.fact: The bark of the spurred mangrove is rich in tannins and has long been used for dyeing and tanning.

entities.name: West African red mangrove
entities.fact: Rhizophora racemosa is the dominant red mangrove along the coast of West Africa.

entities.name: Tea mangrove
entities.fact: The tea mangrove, found on the Pacific coast of the Americas, bears unusually large flowers for a mangrove.

entities.name: Mangrove fern
entities.fact: The mangrove fern is a tall fern that grows at the edges of mangrove forests and can reach several metres in height.

entities.name: Widgeon grass
entities.fact: Widgeon grass grows in salty and brackish water around the world and is eaten by waterfowl.

entities.name: Japanese eelgrass
entities.fact: Japanese eelgrass is native to East Asia and has spread to the Pacific coast of North America.

entities.name: Halophila stipulacea
entities.fact: Halophila stipulacea, native to the Red Sea and Indian Ocean, has spread to the Mediterranean and Caribbean.

entities.name: Paddle grass
entities.fact: Paddle grass can grow in deeper, dimmer water than most seagrasses.

entities.name: Serrated ribbon seagrass
entities.fact: Serrated ribbon seagrass has finely toothed leaf tips and grows in shallow waters across the Indo-West Pacific.

entities.name: Smooth ribbon seagrass
entities.fact: Smooth ribbon seagrass grows in shallow tropical waters of the Indo-West Pacific, often on reef flats.

entities.name: Thalassodendron ciliatum
entities.fact: Thalassodendron ciliatum is a robust seagrass of the Indian Ocean with woody stems that can root into rock.

entities.name: Torrey's surfgrass
entities.fact: Torrey's surfgrass grows on wave-washed rocky shores of the Pacific coast of North America.

entities.name: Cape eelgrass
entities.fact: Cape eelgrass is the main seagrass of South African estuaries.

entities.name: Ribbon weed
entities.fact: A meadow of ribbon weed in Shark Bay, Western Australia, has been found to be a single clone covering about 180 square kilometres.

entities.name: Bath sponge
entities.fact: The soft, springy skeleton of the bath sponge has been harvested from the Mediterranean for thousands of years for washing.

entities.name: Elephant ear sponge
entities.fact: The elephant ear sponge grows as a large, flat fan that can be more than a metre across.

entities.name: Yellow tube sponge
entities.fact: The yellow tube sponge turns dark purple when it is damaged or lifted out of the water.

entities.name: Purple vase sponge
entities.fact: The purple vase sponge grows in tall, vase-shaped tubes on Caribbean reefs.

entities.name: Orange puffball sponge
entities.fact: The orange puffball sponge is a round, orange sponge with a tough surface covered in tiny bumps.

entities.name: Boring sponge
entities.fact: The boring sponge dissolves tunnels into limestone, shells and coral and lives hidden inside them.

entities.name: Golden star tunicate
entities.fact: Colonies of the golden star tunicate form flower-like star shapes, each star made of many linked individuals.

entities.name: Club tunicate
entities.fact: The club tunicate is a club-shaped sea squirt from the north-west Pacific that has invaded coasts and shellfish farms worldwide.

entities.name: Sea peach
entities.fact: The sea peach is a round, orange-red sea squirt of cold North Atlantic and Pacific waters, shaped like a peach.

entities.name: Vase tunicate
entities.fact: The vase tunicate is a see-through, vase-shaped sea squirt widely used in research and invasive in several regions.

entities.name: Violet tunicate
entities.fact: The violet tunicate forms bright, crust-like colonies and has spread as an invader to coasts around the world.

entities.name: Light-bulb tunicate
entities.fact: The light-bulb tunicate lives in clusters of transparent, bulb-shaped bodies attached to rocks and docks.

entities.name: Cloud sponge
entities.fact: Cloud sponges build glass sponge reefs off the coast of British Columbia.

entities.name: Ping-pong tree sponge
entities.fact: The ping-pong tree sponge is a deep-sea carnivorous sponge with branches tipped by ball-shaped structures.

entities.name: Azure vase sponge
entities.fact: The azure vase sponge is a bright blue, vase-shaped sponge of Caribbean reefs.

entities.name: Stinker sponge
entities.fact: The stinker sponge gives off a strong, unpleasant smell when it is out of the water.

entities.name: Touch-me-not sponge
entities.fact: Touching the touch-me-not sponge can cause a painful skin rash.

entities.name: Stove-pipe sponge
entities.fact: The stove-pipe sponge grows in long, slender tubes on Caribbean reefs.

entities.name: Mermaid's glove
entities.fact: Mermaid's glove is a branching sponge of North Atlantic shores whose finger-like lobes give it its name.

entities.name: Carpet sea squirt
entities.fact: The carpet sea squirt spreads over the seabed in smothering mats and is an invader on coasts around the world.

entities.name: Piure
entities.fact: The piure is a red-fleshed sea squirt of the Chilean coast that is eaten as a local delicacy.

entities.name: Red bait
entities.fact: Red bait is a sea squirt of rocky shores in southern Africa and Australia that anglers cut up and use as fishing bait.

entities.name: Sea pineapple
entities.fact: The sea pineapple is a knobbly sea squirt farmed and eaten raw in Japan and Korea.

entities.name: Mangrove tunicate
entities.fact: The mangrove tunicate is the natural source of trabectedin, a compound developed into an anti-cancer drug.

entities.name: Hornwrack
entities.fact: Hornwrack is a bryozoan that forms leaf-like colonies, often washed ashore, with a faint lemon scent.

entities.name: Honeycomb worm
entities.fact: The honeycomb worm builds reefs from sand grains cemented into honeycomb-like tubes.

entities.name: Giant acorn barnacle
entities.fact: The giant acorn barnacle of the North Pacific coast is one of the largest barnacles in the world.

entities.name: Carnivorous sponge
entities.fact: The carnivorous sponge of Mediterranean caves catches tiny crustaceans on hook-covered spicules instead of filtering the water.
